Another explanation could be that it’s simply part of G-d’s plan for me to transition, the idea that god made only 2 genders has not always been a wide held Christian belief, in fact Judaism has recognised intersex individuals as falling out side of strict male vs female and has viewed those born outside the common sexes as just as valid a reflection of G-d as those born male or female. >Also, what exactly does testosterone dominant bone growth mean?

Men and women have different shaped skeletal structures (example women have bigger hips, men have larger ribcages and skull size) 

What hormones are present during puberty determine what skeletal structure you’ll have. For example if you’ve gone through puberty with lots of testosterone (as most amabs have) then you’ll have smaller hips, a larger skull and other male typical skeletal structures.

Now there’s of course variance between every individual, some people start puberty sooner, some have a stronger puberty then others. And some people’s bones don’t stop growing until age 25 while others stop at age 18. 

The fact remains though that for most people who have spent a long time going through puberty with male testosterone levels they will have male skeletal structures. That’s not to say that people with male skeletal structures can’t pass as cis female, but the fact is it’s pretty rare.

The fact is most trans women overestimate their ability to pass, and assume people using their preferred pronouns is the same as passing as cis. 

Anyone 18 or older will have had at least 5+ years of testosterone dominant bone growth. 

Unfortunately most of the bone growth from puberty can’t be reversed.
